FOOD SECURITY 
Tuesdays at the Farm 
Each Tuesday following the 9/11 Day of Service, UMassD students 
attended Dartmouth YMCA’s Sharing the Harvest Community 
Farm to help grow and harvest fresh produce for community 
members experiencing food insecurity. Through the Tuesdays at 
the Farm program, 21 students contributed a total of 56 service 
hours over the course of the year. 
Participants included students from across the university, 
including those enrolled in Professor Sarah Lederman’s SUS 
101: Principles of Sustainability course. By working alongside 
community partners, students gained hands-on experience in 
sustainable agriculture and food systems while helping expand 
access to fresh, healthy food for local families. 
9/11 Day of Service 
Despite driving rain on Sunday, September 7, 150 UMass 
Dartmouth students came together at the YMCA Sharing 
the Harvest Community Farm to help fight food insecurity by 
harvesting butternut squash. Students volunteered in two 
shifts and enjoyed donuts from Black Dog Donuts at the end of 
each shift. By the end of the day, an estimated 11,000 pounds of 
butternut squash was harvested. 
The harvest is part of the YMCA's Sharing the Harvest program, 
which grows fresh produce for South Coast residents. All of 
the food grown at the farm is donated to the United Way of 
Greater New Bedford's Hunger Commission for free distribution 
throughout the region. 
Bristol County was found to be the second most food insecure 
county in the state by a MassInc Polling Group, with 47% of 
residents being nutrition and food insecure. Through initiatives 
like Sharing the Harvest Community Farm, the Dartmouth YMCA 
continues to provide fresh, locally grown food to those in need 
while engaging the community in meaningful service. 
The event is one of many collaborative efforts made possible 
through the nearly 20-year partnership between UMass 
Dartmouth and the YMCA.
